title: Visit the past
concept: git switch --detach; detached HEAD without fear

story.speaker: Sam
story.text: I think I deleted the poster text yesterday. Was it any good?

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: You can look around in the past safely. Find the commit ID from yesterday.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Then type `git switch --detach <commit-ID>` to move your HEAD there.

items.text: Switch to the 'Draft poster text' commit

hints: Run `git log --oneline` to find the commit ID for 'Draft poster text'.
Once you have the ID, move HEAD there with `git switch`.

predict.question: What happens to your files when you switch to an older commit?

choices.text: They instantly change to look exactly as they did back then

predict.explanation: Git changes your working folder to match the past commit you switched to.

recap: `git switch --detach <commit-ID>` lets you look at an old commit. Git calls this a "detached HEAD". You can return to the present later.

cheatSheet.summary: Move HEAD to a past commit to look around
